sourcedFrom: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") (not printed as a © line; the cover carries SEPTEMBER 2016)
cleanIntro: Armscor's 1911 A1/A2 book covers the ROCK Standard FS by name, and its parts list gives the bull barrel only to the 9mm CS among the 9mm pistols, so this full-size 9mm keeps the standard barrel and its barrel bushing. That means the book's own numbered field strip on p.35 applies from start to finish, bushing steps included. The recoil spring plug sits under spring pressure behind the bushing, so keep a thumb on it whenever the bushing is being turned. The book was printed before the stainless version and never names it; stainless is the material of the slide and frame, not a different mechanism.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber checked with the slide back
steps.action: Point it in a safe direction, put your free hand under the magazine so it does not drop, and press the magazine catch. Then pull the slide fully back and look into the chamber. Armscor makes the magazine and the chamber one instruction because a 1911 will still hold a round in the chamber with the magazine out. Keep your finger outside the trigger guard throughout.
steps.aside: Place your free hand under the magazine to prevent it from falling and press the magazine catch to release
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. Pull the slide back and check the chamber to ensure that the pistol is unloaded and safe to handle.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 1, p.35

steps.title: Plug held in, bushing turned clockwise
steps.action: With the slide forward, press the checkered recoil spring plug under the muzzle in with your thumb and hold it there. Then turn the barrel bushing clockwise until its lip no longer covers the plug. The recoil spring is pushing the plug against your thumb the whole time. If your thumb slips, the plug can fly out of the slide, so keep it covered.
steps.quote: Press the recoil spring plug with your thumb and rotate the barrel bushing clockwise.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 2, p.35

steps.title: Plug eased forward, left in place
steps.action: Let the plug come forward slowly under your thumb until the spring has run out of tension. Do not pull it out of the slide yet. Armscor leaves it in at this point because it is what keeps the recoil spring guide in place while you take the slide stop out. A plug that has been eased out is one that cannot jump later.
steps.quote: Slowly allow the plug and recoil spring assembly to move forward. Do not remove yet as this will keep the recoil spring guide in place.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 3, p.35

steps.title: Slide stop pushed out at the disassembly notch
steps.action: Pull the slide back until the lug on the slide stop lines up with the small disassembly notch in the slide, then push the rounded end of the slide stop pin in from the right side of the frame and take the stop out to the left. The stop only passes at the notch. If it will not move, the slide has slipped off the notch, and forcing it will scratch the frame. Hold the slide steady at the notch while you push.
steps.aside: Push inward and through the frame and disengage slide stop from slide and frame.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back until the lug on the slide stop is opposite the disassembly notch and push rounded end of pin of slide stop found at right side of the frame.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 4, p.35

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame, with everything in it
steps.action: Run the slide forward along its rails and off the front of the frame. The barrel, the bushing, the recoil spring, its guide and the plug all come away with the slide. Keep the slide level as it comes clear so the loose plug and spring stay in their tunnel. Do this over a bench.
steps.aside: The barrel, barrel bushing, recoil spring, recoil spring guide and recoil spring plug will come out with it.
steps.quote: Pull the slide forward on its guide rails in the frame.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 5, p.35

steps.title: Recoil spring guide and plug out of the slide
steps.action: With the slide upside down, lift the recoil spring guide out from the back of the spring tunnel, then take the plug and spring out of the front. The spring has no tension on it now, since you let the plug forward earlier. Keep the plug and spring together so they go back in the same way round.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring guide and plug from the slide.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 6, p.35

steps.title: Bushing turned left and pulled out the front
steps.action: Turn the barrel bushing to the left as far as it will go, then pull it straight out of the front of the slide. It only comes out at the end of its turn. If it binds, it is not turned all the way. Do not lever it out with a tool, because the bushing's fit on the barrel is part of how the pistol shoots.
steps.quote: Rotate the barrel bushing to the left as far as it will go and pull it out to the front (this is not applicable for models using a bull-barrel).
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 7, p.35

steps.title: Link tilted forward, barrel out the front
steps.action: Tip the barrel link at the bottom of the barrel forward, toward the muzzle, then slide the barrel out through the front of the slide. With the link folded back it catches inside the slide and the barrel will not pass. Do not force it, just fold the link and try again.
steps.quote: Tilt the barrel link forward to remove the barrel through the front of the slide.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 8, p.35

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Slide, barrel, bushing, recoil spring, guide and plug are all off the frame, and for routine cleaning Armscor stops here. The book's care section says taking off the slide and barrel assembly is enough for normal cleaning. The firing pin and extractor come out in a deeper strip.
steps.quote: Under normal cleaning purposes, field stripping or dismounting of the slide and barrel assembly is sufficient.
steps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Care and Maintenance, p.38

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out under spring pressure
deepSteps.action: Press the firing pin forward with a punch and hold it there, then push the firing pin stop down and off the back of the slide. The pin and its spring push back against your punch the whole time. If you let go before the stop is clear, the pin shoots out of the slide. Point the back of the slide at the bench, not at yourself.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin by pressing it with a pin while pushing the firing pin stop downwards at the same time and out of the slide.
deepSteps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 9, p.35

deepSteps.title: Extractor prised out by its groove
deepSteps.action: The extractor sits in its own tunnel in the slide and was held in by the firing pin stop you just took off. Put a punch into the groove in its rear face and pull it straight back out of the tunnel. Twisting it instead can bend the hook at the front, and a bent extractor needs a gunsmith, not a cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: Pry the extractor with a pin by its groove out of the slide.
deepSteps.cite: 1911 A1/A2 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — September 2016 (the cover block reads "1911 A1/A2 PISTOL SEPTEMBER 2016 USER'S MANUAL") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 10, p.35

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Scrub the bore and chamber with a bore brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Dry-patch the bore until patches come out clean
Wipe the outside of the barrel, its locking lugs and the link

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Scrub the breech face with an old toothbrush and solvent to lift powder and primer residue
Clean inside the slide, the locking lug recesses and the frame and slide rails
Clean around the extractor and the firing pin

cleaning.name: BUSHING, RECOIL SPRING & OIL
tasks: Wipe the barrel bushing inside and out, and the recoil spring, guide and plug
Wipe every part and surface dry so no solvent is left on it
Apply a light film of gun oil to the moving parts straight afterwards

reassembly: To reassemble the pistol, the reverse procedure of disassembly is usually followed.
Slide the barrel back into the slide from the front with the link tilted forward, then push the bushing in from the front and turn it back the way it came out.
Put the recoil spring and plug into the tunnel from the front and the guide in from the rear.
Barrel link must be tilted to the front as far as it can go and make sure the barrel link pin is flush in its seat.
Run the slide back onto the frame rails and refit the slide stop at the disassembly notch.
Press the plug in with your thumb and turn the bushing back counter-clockwise until its lip covers the plug again.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, dry the chamber and bore, cycle the slide and confirm it returns fully into battery, check the slide stop is seated flush and the plug is held behind the bushing, and check the firearm for proper function before loading live ammunition.
